transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-05-27
- Start: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Marta Reyes (Bridgewell CTO), John Patel (Bridgewell Head of ML), Alicia Gomez (Security), Samir Shah (Infra)

Summary: Quick product walkthrough of Redwood's Model Catalog, selecting open models, benchmark results, and compatibility matrices. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private, strong security/compliance requirements (SOC2, KMS), and wants a benchmark run.

Topics: Model catalog UI, API vs Console flows, Redwood Optimize recommendations, model compatibility matrix (quantization, hardware), benchmarks (latency/throughput), security (VPC, KMS, audit logs).

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining — I'm Alex, AE on the account. Priya is our solutions engineer, she'll do the demo and then we'll run through benchmarks and next steps. Marta, thanks for making time.
[00:09] Marta Reyes: Yeah thanks Alex, appreciate it. We wanna see how fast we can get inference into our triage pipeline and what the cost looks like.
[00:17] Priya Singh: Great, I'll share my screen — give a quick nav through the model catalog in the Console and then show the API flow and the Optimize suggestions. We're gonna focus on open models since you mentioned preferring non-proprietary ones.
[00:27] John Patel: Yep, open models or tuned open models are what we're leaning to. Also curious about quantized variants for cost.
[00:33] Priya Singh: Totally. Okay screen's up. So this is the Model Catalog — you can filter by task (generation, chat, embeddings), architecture, tokenization, and importantly by compatibility flags: CPU-friendly, int8/int4 quantization tested, recommended hardware.
[00:47] Priya Singh: Here's an example listing for "Llama-2-13B (quantized)" — note we show a benchmark ribbon with 95th p99 latency on our default hosted cluster, plus throughput at 512-token context. We also surface a compatibility matrix — columns for runtime (TorchServe, Triton-like, Redwood runtime), supported optimizations, and tested quantization profiles.
[01:07] Alex Chen: A small note — sometimes the auto transcript shows "Red wood" in two words, ignore that.
[01:11] John Patel: [laughs] Noted.
[01:13] Priya Singh: Back to catalog — you can click to compare models side-by-side. For Bridgewell's triage use case, we usually recommend a model with strong zero-shot summarization and low tail latency. For that tradeoff, our pick would be a 7B-13B family with int8 quantization on A100 or T4 depending on throughput needs.
[01:32] Marta Reyes: What's the delta in latency and cost between hosted and dedicated? We're sensitive to cost but need predictable latency during peak hours.
[01:39] Priya Singh: Good question. Hosted is great for fast time-to-value; our published catalog numbers are on shared-hosted nodes so you see median latency ~80-120ms p50 for 7B int8 at 128 tokens, p95 ~250ms. Dedicated on reserved A100s can get median down to ~50-70ms p50 and p95 under 150ms with appropriate batching and KV cache warmups. Cost-wise, Dedicated is a monthly reserved commitment but per-token unit cost can be 30-45% lower at high volume. We'll send a more detailed pricing sheet.
[02:04] Samir Shah: For Private deployment, do you support running the same model catalog and telemetry? Our Sec team will want local control.
[02:11] Priya Singh: Yes, Private supports the same control plane and model catalog — it's a customer-managed instance with optional on-prem runtime. We integrate with KMS/HSM, SAML SSO, and our audit logging maps to your SIEM. There are a few caveats: for on-prem you'll want GPUs with the right TF/torch kernels and we'll provide the tested quantization profiles in the compatibility matrix.
[02:31] Alicia Gomez: On audit logs — do you capture per-request metadata and token-level tracing? We need to demonstrate retention and redaction controls for audits.
[02:38] Alex Chen: Short answer: yes. We capture request IDs, model version, route, latency, and token consumption. We also have redaction hooks and can integrate with your KMS for envelope encryption. We'll share our SOC2 + ISO docs and retention policy.
[02:51] John Patel: For the benchmark, what inputs should we provide? We'll want to run our triage traffic pattern — short prompts, sometimes longer context.
[02:58] Priya Singh: Best practice: give us a sample of 1,000 representative requests across token lengths, and specify latency SLOs (p95 target). We'll run a side-by-side with a 7B int8, 13B int8, and a high-accuracy FP16 13B, then produce a comparison CSV: p50/p95/p99, throughput (tokens/sec), and cost per 1M tokens estimate.
[03:18] Marta Reyes: Sounds good. Also, how do you handle model fallbacks? Suppose dedicated capacity spikes and we need graceful degradation.
[03:25] Priya Singh: The Smart Routing policy can fallback to a compatible hosted model or lower-tier quantized variant. You define policy: latency-first, cost-first, or hybrid. We also support circuit-breaker thresholds and can do canary rollouts.
[03:36] Alex Chen: Quick demo switch — API. This is the same flow as Console but via REST. If you embed in your triage pipeline you call POST /v1/generate with model id, input, and optional route hints (e.g., prefer_dedicated:true). Response streaming is supported.
[03:52] John Patel: Does streaming increase token costs or change latency?
[03:55] Priya Singh: Streaming doesn't change token billing; it can improve perceived latency for UX by returning partial tokens. For our internal benchmarks, we measure both end-to-end completion and first-byte latency.
[04:07] Marta Reyes: When you say "compatibility matrix", can you show an example row?
[04:12] Priya Singh: Sure. Example: model: "ggml-7b-int4"; runtime tested: Redwood runtime v2.1 (xg), TorchServe (community); quantization: int4 tested w/ 64K context; recommended hardware: T4/3090 for low-cost inference; notes: limited QA on extreme-long context, recommended for short summaries.
[04:34] John Patel: Interesting — we have a lot of long-context passes. Any support for long-form KV cache management?
[04:40] Priya Singh: Yes, the runtime supports KV cache sharding and prefix-caching. For long context workloads we recommend models with longer sequence support and specific kernel-selection that the catalog indicates. The Optimize page will surface batching + cache suggestions based on observed traffic.
[04:55] Alex Chen: Quick aside — sometimes model names in the catalog are slightly off in transcription — e.g., "llama" vs "lama", ignore that.
[05:00] [brief chuckle]
[05:03] Priya Singh: Next I'm gonna open Redwood Optimize — this is the cost/performance toolkit. You can upload a sample traffic trace and it will recommend batching window, cache TTLs, quantization profile, and suggest which models in the catalog match your accuracy/latency targets.
[05:17] Priya Singh: For Bridgewell's sample trace we uploaded earlier (demo data), Optimize recommended a 20ms batching window for small bursts and int8 profile for 7B family. It also proposed a hybrid routing: dedicated for business-hours peak, hosted burst for off-hours.
[05:31] Marta Reyes: Can Optimize produce A/B suggestions and guardrails for rollout? We want to avoid regressions in triage accuracy.
[05:36] Priya Singh: Yes, rollouts support canary groups and metric-based guardrails. You can tie evaluations to prompt sets — if accuracy drops by more than X% on the eval set we can automatically rollback. We also have evaluation dashboards that show per-prompt diffs.
[05:48] John Patel: Any limitations re: custom fine-tunes or instruction-tuning artifacts? We often add a small instruction-tuned head.
[05:55] Priya Singh: You can bring your own fine-tuned model artifacts; the catalog supports custom model entries and we can run the same compatibility tests. For private/on-prem there are extra onboarding steps for weights transfer and kernel compatibility.
[06:07] Samir Shah: Regarding network — for Private, do you require outbound to Redwood control plane for telemetry? We prefer minimal egress.
[06:14] Priya Singh: You can opt into a control-plane-less on-prem deployment where telemetry is stored locally. There is an option for a private control plane inside your VPC with peered connectivity. We'll include the network diagram in the security package.
[06:27] Alicia Gomez: KMS integration — do you support AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and HSM?
[06:31] Alex Chen: Yes to AWS KMS and Azure KV; HSM via SOAP — sorry, HSM via PKCS11 integrations and we also support bring-your-own-HSM. We'll include the integration guide.
[06:40] Alicia Gomez: Good. Also need to confirm data residency — logs and telemetry retention.
[06:44] Priya Singh: Retention is configurable per account; defaults are 90 days but we can extend with enterprise add-on. Audit exports in CSV/JSON can be pushed to your S3 or GCS.
[06:54] John Patel: Back to benchmarks — can you show a sample benchmark artifact?
[06:58] Priya Singh: Yep — pulling a sample CSV. Shows columns: model_id, hardware, context_length, p50_ms, p95_ms, tokens_per_sec, cost_per_1M. For a quick example: 7B-int8 on T4: p50 85ms p95 240ms throughput 1200 tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens $12 (demo numbers). 13B-int8 on A100: p50 120ms p95 310ms, 2200 tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens $18. These are illustrative. We'll run with your real traces for accurate numbers.
[07:38] Marta Reyes: Okay that gives us a baseline. Can you also include the compatibility matrix in a spreadsheet? Our infra team will map it to our hardware.
[07:46] Alex Chen: Yes we will include that as a CSV attachment.
[07:49] Priya Singh: Quick note — there may be small naming mismatches in the transcript export (e.g., "KV cache" becomes "K V cache" in some exports).
[07:56] John Patel: [laughs] transcripts are always weird.
[08:00] Alex Chen: Alright let's move to wrap up. Recap of action items: we'll share pricing, SOC2/ISO docs, benchmark template, and schedule the benchmark run. Can everyone confirm availability next week for the benchmark kickoff?
[08:15] Marta Reyes: Tuesday morning works for us.
[08:18] John Patel: Tuesday 10am PT works.
[08:20] Samir Shah: Works.
[08:21] Alicia Gomez: Works for security to be in the sync.
[08:23] Alex Chen: Great — I'll send calendar invite for Tue 2026-06-02 10:00 PT. Priya will own the benchmark execution, I'll follow up with pricing.
[08:31] Marta Reyes: One last quick Q: any gotchas with model license terms for open models? We need to ensure compliance.
[08:36] Priya Singh: We surface license labels in the catalog and flag models with restrictive terms. We'll include a summary of license constraints for the models we propose.
[08:45] Alex Chen: Perfect. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the materials and the invite.
[08:50] [meeting ends]

End of transcript.
